data.content_ref: inline:SRC_004's information-theoretic isolation mechanism claims functional independence if the checker reconstructs logic from scratch and it matches the claim. But mere reconstruction matching is not causal evidence of verification: a second engine can reproduce a false derivation by coincidence or by following the same flawed inference. The target gives no executable or countable criterion—e.g., running the reconstruction against held-out tests—to distinguish genuine verification from restatement.
